Decide your wedding priorities together, two at a time

Wedding budgets go wrong when every line feels essential. Picking which of two things matters more is quick, and doing it separately shows each of you what the other actually cares about before the deposits go down.

Start ranking this list →

Opens the free ranker with the list below already filled in. Change it there with "Start over", or paste your own list.

The starter list

Question: "Which matters more for our wedding?"

  1. The venue
  2. Photography
  3. Food and drink
  4. Inviting everyone we want
  5. Music or a band
  6. Flowers and decor
  7. The dress or suit
  8. A honeymoon
  9. Video
  10. The date we want
  11. Staying within budget
  12. Guests' travel being easy

Why picking pairs works here

  • You each answer alone on your own phone, then paste each other's result codes to see one combined order and the items you rank far apart.
  • Each item's best-to-worst place across the two of you points straight at the conversation to have.
  • Nothing is uploaded: the list travels in the link and your answers stay in your browser.

What it doesn't do: It ranks what you care about, not what things cost. Use the order to decide where the money goes, then price it.

Compared with what you'd use today

Wedding budget worksheets, planning apps with checklists, or a long talk. A worksheet starts from costs; this starts from what each of you would give up first.

Under the hood: a Bradley-Terry model refit after every answer, an adaptive question picker, and a stop rule checked against simulated respondents, including ones whose picks are close calls. The method and its measurements.
